spec.sourceRegion: Question 6, lower portion of printed page 399.
spec.description: Two right triangles share a horizontal base and vertical right side. An internal segment meets the vertical side below the upper vertex. The upper vertical section has a double-headed dimension arrow.
spec.mathematics: Base 10 m; outer hypotenuse d m; lower-left sectors 45 degrees and 15 degrees; lower-right angle 90 degrees; upper vertical section x m. Coordinates derive the internal and outer rays at 45 and 60 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels appear; no calculated angle or length is supplied.

children.prompt: For the diagram shown below, find the value of $d$.

answer.worked:
The angle between the base and the outer hypotenuse is $45^{\circ}+15^{\circ}=60^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}\cos60^{\circ}&=\frac{10}{d}\\d\cos60^{\circ}&=10\\d&=\frac{10}{\cos60^{\circ}}\\d&=\frac{10}{1/2}\\d&=20\ \mathrm{m}\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$x=10(\sqrt{3}-1)\ \mathrm{m}$.

Subtract the smaller triangle’s height from the larger triangle’s height.
answer.worked:
Let $H$ be the total vertical height and $h$ the lower vertical height, both measured in metres.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{H}{10}&=\tan60^{\circ}\\H&=10\tan60^{\circ}\\H&=10\sqrt{3}\\\frac{h}{10}&=\tan45^{\circ}\\h&=10\tan45^{\circ}\\h&=10\\x&=H-h\\x&=10\sqrt{3}-10\\x&=10(\sqrt{3}-1)\end{align*}$$
Hence the upper vertical section is $10(\sqrt{3}-1)\ \mathrm{m}$.
